first.rationale: Two internal metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are degrading simultaneously and are within our control, whereas the competitor's aggressive pricing move is an external shock whose long-term effect on qualified revenue is uncertain—matching price cuts risks a margin-eroding race to the bottom and attracting lower-quality, price-sensitive accounts (memory_73's SMB context may not generalize to a competitive price-war scenario, hence flagging it for verification and as a risk rather than acting on it now). Memories 31 and 86 both point to onboarding/signup simplification driving durable activation gains for self-serve/SMB accounts, directly addressing the two declining metrics with a lower-risk, more controllable lever. I verify memory_86 (most directly tied to the onboarding completion drop) and memory_73 (to check whether its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' claim holds up against sustainability concerns before ruling it out this cycle). With only one experiment slot, simplify_onboarding offers the best expected sustainable qualified-revenue impact this week, while promotional pricing is deferred pending better evidence on long-term account quality effects.
